findings.evidence: Artin.lean:282-283 `let _ : Invertible (Nat.card C : k) := (isUnit_natCard_subgroup C (isUnit_of_invertible _)).invertible` is the only use of the `Invertible (Nat.card G : k)` instance in the proof; the remaining steps (`virtualCharacters_eq_closure_irreducibleCharacters`, CharacterTable/VirtualCharacter.lean:216-248) need `[IsAlgClosed k]`, `[Finite C]` and `[Invertible (Nat.card C : k)]` only. `isUnit_natCard_subgroup (S : Subgroup G) (hG : IsUnit (Nat.card G : k))` (GroupTheory/Index.lean:169) goes one way only. The exactly parallel comparison in Spanning.lean:292 already takes `(h𝒮 : ∀ S ∈ 𝒮, IsUnit (Nat.card S : k))` and its docstring (Spanning.lean:289-291) states: "Only the orders of the *selected* subgroups need be invertible in `k`; `|G|` itself is irrelevant here"; likewise `indCharacterSpan_eq_indSpan` (Spanning.lean:312).
findings.fix: Replace the instance argument by the hypothesis used one file over: `theorem indVirtualCharacters_le_indVirtualCharacterSpan [IsAlgClosed k] {𝒮 : Set (Subgroup G)} (h𝒮 : ∀ S ∈ 𝒮, IsUnit (Nat.card S : k))`, deriving the local instance as `let _ : Invertible (Nat.card C : k) := (h𝒮 C hC).invertible`; propagate the same signature to `indVirtualCharacters_eq_indVirtualCharacterSpan` and update the two docstrings (:271, :301) accordingly. Cyclic-family callers supply `fun S _ ↦ isUnit_natCard_subgroup S (isUnit_of_invertible _)`.
findings.issue: `indVirtualCharacters_le_indVirtualCharacterSpan` (:278-283) assumes `[Invertible (Nat.card G : k)]`, but `|G|` is used only to manufacture `Invertible (Nat.card C : k)` for the C ∈ 𝒮 actually being induced from (line 282-283). The hypothesis is strictly stronger: for G = S₃, k of characteristic 3 and 𝒮 the 2-Sylow subgroups, every |C| = 2 is invertible while |G| = 6 is not, so the theorem is unavailable in a case it covers. Same over-assumption on `indVirtualCharacters_eq_indVirtualCharacterSpan` (:305-307), which only forwards it.

summary: The family-generalization of indVirtualCharacterSpan is done and the bundled direct-sum/base-change API sits at the right level. One over-strong hypothesis remains: the two comparison theorems assume |G| invertible where only the orders of the selected subgroups are used, contradicting the weaker convention already established for the same comparison in Spanning.lean.
